title: Pacing strategy patterns and performance outcomes in marathon running: A large-scale analysis of split time data
claims: Split times from 78,912 Boston Marathon finishers (2015–2017) were analyzed at nine checkpoints from 5K through 40K, converting cumulative times into segment times and segment paces.

Cluster analysis identified four patterns: even-pacing (47.9%), mild positive-splitting (31.9%), strong positive-splitting (12.2%) and variable-pacing (8.0%); even-pacing was associated with the fastest finish times.

A pace decline above 20% in the final segment defines hitting the wall in this analysis; variable-pacing runners showed the highest such incidence, and sub-3:00 runners paced even far more often than casual participants.
